title: The Glorious Flamingo
summary: Josh and Chuck explore flamingos: their taxonomic order (Phoenicopteriformes) and the shift from old looks-based classification to genetics (closest relative the grebe, per a 2001 finding), the five species (Greater, Caribbean/American, Chilean, Lesser, Andean, plus James's flamingo) and their distribution and habitats in saline/alkaline lakes, why they are pink (carotenoids from algae and crustaceans converted in the liver to pigment), filter feeding, lifespan (oldest on record Greater flamingo, 83, at Adelaide Zoo, who was beaten by teenagers in 2008), migration and night flights, standing on one leg, mating dances and the "disco finger," monogamous pairing, crop milk, chick rearing, same-sex pair Freddie Mercury and Lance Bass at the Denver Zoo, cave art and historical hunting for feathers and food, Florida origins of the Caribbean flamingo, zoo tricks like mirrors, escaped flamingo Pink Floyd in Salt Lake City, and a listener mail segment about a cat's silver coat (fever coat). Also includes tour announcements and a Bible Time Machine plug.

segments.title: Opening banter and flamingo parade in the Bahamas
segments.summary: Josh recounts visiting flamingos in the Bahamas, the morning flamingo parade, and a video artist's flamingo bowing video. Hosts banter about the flamingo painting and their interest in the birds.

segments.title: Flamingo taxonomy and classification
segments.summary: The order Phoenicopteriformes is discussed, along with older classification by appearance (storks, herons, geese, ducks) and the 2001 genetic finding that the closest relative is the grebe.

segments.title: Name origin and the species list
segments.summary: The word flamingo's Spanish link to flamenco is noted. Hosts begin the species discussion, with Greater flamingo, Caribbean flamingo as subspecies debate, and their distribution in Africa, Europe, and Asia.

segments.title: Chilean, Lesser, and Andean flamingos
segments.summary: Descriptions of the Chilean flamingo, the smallest Lesser flamingo, and the rare Andean flamingo that lives high in the Andes and is threatened by lithium mining and climate change.

segments.title: James's flamingo
segments.summary: James's flamingo was thought extinct in the 1920s, then rediscovered in the 1950s mixed in with Chilean and Andean flocks; it is named after naturalist Harry Berkeley James.

segments.title: Break and tour announcements
segments.summary: Break, then hosts discuss upcoming live shows and the chosen cities, plus a Bible Time Machine podcast plug.

segments.title: Why flamingos are pink
segments.summary: Flamingos get their pink color from carotenoids in algae and small organisms, which the liver converts into pigment that ends up in feathers and skin. Filter feeding with upside-down bills is described, and zoos feeding carrots and peppers is noted.

segments.title: Flamingo lifespan and the Adelaide Zoo attack
segments.summary: Flamingos live twenty to sixty years; the oldest on record, a Greater flamingo named Greater at the Adelaide Zoo, lived to 83 and was beaten by teenagers in 2008.

segments.title: Migration and standing on one leg
segments.summary: Flamingos are considered non-migratory but may fly at night 300 to 400 miles to find better habitat. Theories on why they stand on one leg are discussed, including heat conservation (ruled out) and locking leg joints for stability; the knee is up near the hip.

segments.title: Flamingo social life, mating dances, and parenting
segments.summary: Flamingos form flocks called flamboyances, have complex social groups, are peaceful, and are serial monogamous. Mating dances include the disco finger. Both sexes help incubate one egg and produce crop milk; chicks go to crèches.

segments.title: Same-sex flamingo pairs and flamingo culture history
segments.summary: Denver Zoo same-sex pair Freddie Mercury and Lance Bass; flamingos appear in cave art seven thousand years old in southern Spain and in Egyptian art and kids books. Historical hunting for feathers and food, including in ancient Rome, is covered.

segments.title: Florida flamingos, zoo mirrors, and Pink Floyd the escaped flamingo
segments.summary: The Caribbean flamingo is found native to South Florida; Conky was tagged. Zoos use mirrors to make small flocks breed; Pink Floyd escaped from the Tracy Aviary and lived at the Great Salt Lake. Eating flamingos and Pliny the Elder's comments are also covered.

segments.title: Listener mail: cat silver coat mystery
segments.summary: Listener Sarah Patton explains the silver coat of Josh's cat Lauren may be a fever coat from the mother having a fever during pregnancy.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts close with a reminder to listen to the short stuff episode on pink flamingo lawn ornaments and invite listener email.
